Subject: Security & retention next steps for Redwood pilot (post-call recap)

Hi Miguel —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call plus concrete next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of pain & goals
- Pain: existing inference infra has inconsistent audit logs (varying retention / indexing across services) and unpredictable tail-latency for batch settlement flows.
- Goal: a pilot that demonstrates consistent 99th percentile latency < 150ms for user-facing flows, and an auditable retention/profile for audit logs to meet internal controls.
- Compliance ask: SOC 2 attestation, pen test summary, DPA language around retention and deletion, and a detailed mapping of what audit events Redwood persists (auth, model input hashes, admin actions, inference logs).

Action items (owners + timing)
1) Redwood: share SOC 2 summary + high-level pen test findings (attachment: redwood_soc2_summary_v1.pdf) — by Tue 7/6 (owner: me).
2) Clearwater: share security questionnaire and legal contact for DPA redlines (owner: Miguel / Ellie) — requested in this thread.
3) Redwood SE: fill out the security questionnaire with field-level mapping for logs & retention (attachment: rdw_response_matrix_v0.2.xlsx) — by Fri 7/9 (owner: Dev).
4) Technical sync to walk through audit log schema and infra controls (30–45m) — propose Wed 7/7 or Thu 7/8.
5) Procurement: share procurement timeline and PO process (owner: procurement@clearwaterbank.com).

Open questions we flagged on the call
- Minimum acceptable retention window for audit logs and whether there are specific immutable storage requirements.
- Whether ClearWater requires encrypted-at-rest + HSM-managed keys for customer-supplied models.
- Expected SLA for dedicated capacity during pilot (we can table this until discovery is complete but wanted it recorded).

Attachments in this email: redwood_soc2_summary_v1.pdf (high-level), response matrix template (rdw_response_matrix_v0.2.xlsx).

Next steps I suggest: Miguel/Legal confirm who will own DPA redlines; Dev and I will start populating the questionnaire and schedule the technical sync once we get the availability.

Thanks — feel free to correct anything I missed.

—
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0184
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Security & retention next steps for Redwood pilot (post-call recap)

Thanks Jasmine — that matches our notes. A few clarifications and next steps from our side: 

- I'll loop in Ellie Wu (legal) for DPA redlines — Ellie, copying you for visibility. Please expect standard banking DPA asks: data residency clauses, breach notification timelines, and minimum retention controls.
- Procurement: our target for vendor selection is EoQ (end of July); procurement@clearwaterbank.com will share the formal timeline and PO template.
- Regarding retention: our initial requirement is 7 years for audit artifacts tied to financial transactions; for inference inputs we may relax this to 2 years if we can demonstrate hashing + re-identification controls. We need a mapping of what Redwood persists and where.

Attached is our filled security questionnaire (clearwater_security_questionnaire.xlsx) — we've left a few fields blank for your SE to confirm. Also copying a short list of required evidence:
- SOC 2 report (or SOC 2 summary if repo can't be shared yet)
- Pen test executive summary and remediation timeline
- Audit log schema + retention policy

Happy to schedule the technical sync on Wed 7/7 11:00am PT — that works for our infra lead.

Best,
Miguel

Head of Cloud Engineering
Clearwater Bank

Miguel / team — thanks for the questionnaire. I started filling the matrix; attaching the working draft (rdw_response_matrix_v0.2.xlsx). Highlights / quick answers inline below for the items you flagged: 

- Audit events persisted: auth.success, auth.failure, token_issuance, model.inference.request (headers + model-id + input-hash), model.inference.response (token count, latency, model-variant), admin.changes (user, timestamp, change-delta).
- Retention options: per-customer retention policies are configurable; default is 90 days for raw inputs, 2 years for inferred artifacts (hashes + metadata), with an archival tier to meet longer-term retention for gated accounts. We can configure immutable retention buckets for compliance-backed archives.
- Encryption: all data at rest is AES-256; for customers requiring HSM KMS we support BYOK with KMS integration (we'll share KMS integration notes in the drive).
- Pen test: we cannot share full reports publicly, but redwood_soc2_summary_v1.pdf contains the executive summary and remediation status. Full reports can be shared under NDA.

I can run through the response matrix on Wed 7/7 at 11:00am PT (works for me) and demo the audit log schema. Proposed agenda for the 30m call: 1) quick mapping of question -> evidence; 2) walk audit log fields; 3) confirm retention buckets & archival options.

Regards,
Dev Patel
